subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class hard tool policy for cron jobs, and should that be an explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` layer or inheritance from `tools.subagents.tools`?
rationale: This chooses a public config contract and security boundary for scheduled automation, including how it composes with existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, so automation should not pick the permanent semantics.

options.title: Add Explicit Cron Tool Policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence, schema/types/help/docs metadata, and tests for message-tool denial across cron delivery modes.

options.title: Make Cron Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Treat cron sessions as part of the existing subagent policy path, which avoids another config block but may blur two different runtime identities.

options.title: Keep Only Per-Job `toolsAllow`
options.body: Decline a global cron default and document per-job `--tools` as the supported enforcement mechanism, accepting that operators must configure each job separately.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Cron Tool Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence, schema/types/help/docs metadata, and tests for message-tool denial across cron delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the config/tool-policy files and the prior maintainer-facing review for this issue.
